title: Homogeneity in Model Predictions Under Covariate Shift

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if all models share the same demographic blind spots, portfolio diversity does not protect marginalized groups. Directly relevant to AI safety equity and fairness concerns.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: BBQ, WinoBias, and HateXplain are publicly available with documented evaluation procedures. Subgroup error analysis is a standard fairness evaluation technique accessible to CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: run existing benchmarks on 10+ models, compute per-subgroup error rates, measure inter-model correlation. Reuses established evaluation infrastructure. Completable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: LLM bias and fairness across models is extensively studied. The comprehensive survey 'Bias and Fairness in Large Language Models' (Computational Linguistics, MIT Press 2024) documents pervasive and systematic biases. The AI Bias Report 2025 shows shared patterns: all tested models linked AAE terms to negative stereotypes. BBQ, WinoBias, and HateXplain benchmarks exist with documented evaluation procedures. However, the specific framing of whether all models share the same demographic blind spots — making portfolio diversity ineffective for fairness — has not been systematically studied as a homogeneity/correlation question. Existing work evaluates bias per model; the inter-model correlation of per-subgroup error rates is a partially addressed gap.
